content:
Anna (CS): Quick sync on AcmePay onboarding — flagged medium renewal risk. Onboarding at ~75% (prod tests pending). Their biggest blocker is unit cost: current per-1M token bill is higher than their projection.

Anna (CS): Proactive recs we should try before renewal conversation: quantize their primary chat model to int8 for non-sensitive routes, swap heavy reranker to a pruned/quantized variant, and route long-horizon (>512 tokens) requests to a dedicated pool with aggressive batching. Expect ~30-45% cost reduction in those flows with minimal quality loss. @Dave @Maria @Sam thoughts?

Dave (Eng): SGTM. Can we run a 24h shadow test (staging) of int8 quantized model to collect latency and perf histograms? Also enable prefix KV caching for chat to reduce decode cost.

Maria (ML): I'll run the eval on AcmePay's top-10 prompts + hallucination-sensitive set. If quality delta is <2% (task metric) or within business tolerance, we'll approve int8. Suggest model swap options: base-7B -> quant-7B-q8 OR base-13B -> pruned-13B-q4 for reranker to keep recall.

Sam (Platform): Routing policy idea: send requests with token_count >=512 to dedicated_pool with batching and lower preemption. Example policy (pseudo-config):

```
route_policy: 
  - name: acmepay-long-horizon
    match: request.tokens >= 512
    target: dedicated-pool-acmepay
    batching: {max_batch: 32, timeout_ms: 25}
    fallback: hosted-lowcost
    metrics: {slo_p50_ms: 150, alert_on_error_rate: 0.02}
```

Sam (Platform): We can also set a model-variant mapping: chat -> quant-7B-q8 (non-sensitive), chat-sensitive -> base-7B (no quant), reranker -> pruned-13B-q4.

Anna (CS): I'll prep a one-pager for AcmePay CSM + account owner: expected cost savings, perf tradeoffs, test plan, and rollback. Need a simple chart to show cost delta.

Dave (Eng): I'll implement a canary rollout: 5% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback triggers (latency > 200ms OR error-rate +1.5x). Also add request-level sampling for quality review.

Maria (ML): Sending eval artifacts by EOD. If all green I'll tag model artifacts with `acmepay-q8` and publish to the model catalog (staging).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot uploaded quantization-runner to staging cluster — job r-54321 started.

Sam (Platform): I'll provision the dedicated pool (n1-gpu-4x) for the test window and attach the routing policy. SLO target p50=150ms.

Anna (CS): :thumbsup: Action items: Maria -> run evals + post artifacts; Dave -> configure canary + rollback; Sam -> provision pool + routing; Anna -> draft one-pager + schedule enablement call with AcmePay and CSMs (tentatively Tue). I'll capture customer feedback in Gainsight and paste the summary here.

Anna (CS): One more ask — can someone add a small example snippet for the customer showing how to pin model variants in their app? A tiny code example will help their engineers adopt the swap.

Dave (Eng): Will do, adding snippet to the one-pager and linking to the internal runbook: https://redwood.internal/docs/perf/quantization-playbook

Maria (ML): If we see any quality regressions, fallback plan is immediate route back to base model variant and mark a rollback in the console for audit.

Anna (CS): Thanks team. If the staging shadow test hits the savings we expect, I’ll push the renewal discussion with numbers.

Sam (Platform): Noted — provisioning now. I’ll post pool details when ready.

Anna (CS): tagging for visibility: @Dave (Eng) @Maria (ML) @Sam (Platform) — will follow up in this thread with test results and the one-pager link.
